title: Add incident_type to alert payloads and use it for pager routing (with unknown fallback)
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Reliability Program — Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping
description:
Problem:
Today, most automated alerts page either (a) the SRE on-call by default, or (b) a static service-based PD route. As we roll out the v1 incident taxonomy + owner mapping, we need alerts to carry a structured incident_type and to route pages to the primary owning team when safe. This reduces time-to-mitigate by paging the team with operational control, and creates consistency between alerting, incident-bot, and reporting.

Scope:
- Add incident_type (and optionally incident_subtype where available) to internal alert payload schema emitted by redwood services.
- Update paging logic to route to owner team PD service based on incident_type mapping.
- Implement explicit fallback behavior when incident_type is missing/unknown/unclassified.
- Preserve a low-cardinality approach (incident_type only in alert payload; avoid incident_subtype in high-volume labels).

Non-goals:
- Redesign of severity classification (Sev0/1/2 continues to be driven by alert policy + IC judgment).
- Full automatic incident creation from every alert (we’ll keep existing thresholds/aggregation).
acceptance_criteria: Alert payload schema includes incident_type field (string, allowlist enforced at emit or ingestion).
Pager routing selects the primary owner PD service for allowlisted incident_type values.
Unknown/missing incident_type routes to SRE primary (with clear annotation so on-call can reclassify).
Routing decision is visible in payload/annotations (e.g., routed_owner_team, routing_reason).
No material increase in alert cardinality / storage cost (validated by Observability review).
Rollback is possible (feature flag or config revert) without redeploying all services.
implementation_notes:
Design summary:
1) Schema:
- Add fields to the alert payload envelope used by our internal alert pipeline:
  - incident_type: one of the taxonomy top-level types (e.g., AVAILABILITY_OVERLOAD, LATENCY_REGRESSION, STREAMING_DISCONNECTS, ROUTING_FALLBACK_MISBEHAVIOR, CONTROL_PLANE_OUTAGE, AUTH_RBAC_FAILURE, TELEMETRY_BLIND_SPOT, CAPACITY_FLEET_SHORTAGE, PRIVATE_CONNECTIVITY_CONFIG)
  - incident_subtype: optional; only populated when the emitter has high confidence (not used for routing in v1)
  - routed_owner_team: resolved by router at paging time
  - routing_reason: {type_mapped | type_missing | type_unknown | mapping_missing | safety_fallback}

2) Routing:
- Pager router consumes incident_type from alert payload and resolves owner via the control-plane owner mapping config (ENG-4825).
- Routing happens only for PD pages (not for low-sev Slack-only notifications).
- If the mapping points to a team without a PD service configured, fallback to SRE primary + include mapping_missing annotation.

3) Safety fallback rules (v1):
- If incident_type is missing/empty: route to SRE primary.
- If incident_type is present but not in allowlist: route to SRE primary and set routing_reason=type_unknown.
- If incident_type indicates TELEMETRY_BLIND_SPOT: still route to Observability primary *only* when the alert source is Observability-owned (to avoid routing real outages incorrectly). Otherwise fallback to SRE.
- If incident_type indicates SECURITY-related auth anomalies (AUTH_RBAC_FAILURE with suspicious characteristics): continue to page SRE primary and also notify Security Ops via Slack signal; do not auto-page Security PD from this ticket (per Security Ops alignment).

4) Cardinality guardrails:
- incident_type is attached at the payload level; we do not add incident_subtype as a metric label to high-volume timeseries.
- Router will emit a single counter for routing outcomes (by routing_reason + incident_type bucket, with unknown collapsed).

5) Ownership source-of-truth:
- Owner mapping is read from control plane config (versioned + auditable). In an emergency, SRE can temporarily override mapping to force pages to SRE or to a single team during an incident.

Open choice we made:
- We will not route based purely on service name; incident_type must be set OR the alert policy explicitly opts into a service-based route. This prevents accidental paging of the wrong team when services are shared across tiers.
test_plan:
Unit tests:
- Payload schema migration: backwards compatibility (older senders, newer router).
- Routing function: table-driven tests for each fallback case.
- Allowlist enforcement: unknown incident_type -> SRE + routing_reason=type_unknown.

Integration tests:
- Synthetic alert injected into staging pipeline for each incident_type; verify PD route selection.
- Verify Slack notification includes incident_type + routed_owner_team.

Canary:
- Enable incident_type-based routing for 10% of alerts in staging for 48 hours.
- Production canary limited to non-Sev0 policies for first 72 hours; then expand to Sev0/1 once validated.

Monitoring:
- New dashboard panel: routing_reason counts over time, % fallback to SRE, top incident_type routed.
- Pager audit logs sampled to ensure routed_owner_team matches mapping config.
rollout_plan:
Step 0: Merge payload schema changes (backwards compatible) and deploy router changes behind flag.
Step 1: Populate incident_type in a small set of high-signal alerts (overload, routing fallback, control-plane write failures).
Step 2: Turn on routing in staging; verify PD pages go to expected on-call services.
Step 3: Production canary with flag + allowlist limited to 3 incident types:
- CAPACITY_FLEET_SHORTAGE -> Fleet PD
- ROUTING_FALLBACK_MISBEHAVIOR -> Routing PD
- CONTROL_PLANE_OUTAGE -> Platform Control Plane PD
Step 4: Expand allowlist to all v1 types once owner mapping config is finalized.
Step 5: Announce in #eng-sre + on-call training; document how to override if misrouted.
Rollback: Disable routing flag (router defaults to SRE). If mapping itself is wrong, revert config to previous version in control plane.
open_questions: Do we want to page Support/CS ever based on incident_type (e.g., Dedicated customer-impact)? For v1: no, only notify via Slack + handoff.
Should we treat Dedicated/Private tier differently for routing? For v1: routing is owner-team based; tier affects severity/SLAs, not who gets paged.
Should incident_subtype ever influence routing? For v1: no (keeps rules stable and low-risk).
comments: 2025-12-06 — Allison Grant: Please do NOT add incident_subtype as an Alertmanager label; payload field is fine. For metrics, collapse unknown/unclassified into a single bucket. Also make sure allowlist enforcement happens before PagerDuty integration to avoid freeform strings.

2025-12-08 — Mina Haddad: Routing team PD service naming is inconsistent across regions. Suggest mapping to a stable team identifier first, then lookup PD service per region. If too big for v1, fall back to global team PD service and include region in page body.

2025-12-10 — Ethan Park: Owner mapping config in control plane will provide type->primary team as a stable key. You can depend on that, but please include mapping version in router logs for audit/debug.

2025-12-12 — Rafael Mendes: Priority P0. Misrouted pages are worse than slower pages. Default to SRE when any uncertainty. Also ensure incident commander can re-route within incident-bot if we detect wrong owner during the incident.

2026-01-07 — Sergio Costa: Staging canary looked good. One issue: a subset of alerts were missing incident_type because they go through legacy pipeline. We should add a migration task later, but fallback to SRE is working as designed.

2026-01-15 — Dylan Brooks: Production canary expanded to include Sev1 policies. Observed ~18% SRE fallback due to missing incident_type on a few older alerts; no incorrect routes found. Added routed_owner_team + routing_reason into PD details + Slack attachment.
changelog: 2025-12-05: Ticket created; initial design drafted with payload schema + routing fallback rules.
2025-12-13: Added allowlist enforcement + observability guardrails per review feedback.
2026-01-08: Staging canary completed; fixed legacy pipeline behavior by keeping fallback to SRE and surfacing routing_reason.
2026-01-18: Production rollout complete for v1 allowlisted types; documented rollback + on-call guidance; marked Done.
